title: Provenance manifest for a geospatial dataset
description: One record, written next to one output dataset, complete enough that someone who was not there can re-run the operation and disagree with it. A manifest records what was done; it does not certify that it was right — those are different claims, and this format only makes the first.

spec_version.description: The version of this specification the record conforms to. Semantic versioning; this schema accepts any 1.x.y. A record without it cannot be interpreted once the format has more than one version, which is why it is the one field that can never be optional.

operation.description: What was done, as a stable identifier (e.g. `watershed`, `buffer_layer`). Producers choose their own vocabulary; consumers must not assume one.

parameters.description: The exact parameters the engine ran with — not the ones requested, the ones used. May be empty, but must be present: an absent field cannot be told apart from 'nobody recorded them'.

inputs.description: Every dataset the operation read. May be empty for pure generators. Order is not significant.

path.description: Where the input lived, with `/` as the only separator on every platform. A path that carries the host's separator makes two manifests for the same run differ in a field that describes nothing about the computation. Recorded as given (relative stays relative, absolute stays absolute): rewriting it would misstate what ran.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the input's bytes, lowercase hex. The bytes, not the filename: a manifest whose input has been edited since stops matching, and says so. For a shapefile or a `.gdb` directory, since 1.0.0-draft.9, the SHA-256 of the listing of its member files that section 3.3 defines.

crs.description: The input's coordinate reference system as a short label (e.g. `EPSG:32610`), or null when it has none. A label, not an identity: consumers comparing coordinate systems need the datasets, not this string.

layer.description: The layer read, for container formats holding more than one. Without it, an auditor holding a five-layer container and this record cannot tell which layer produced the numbers.

argument.description: Since 1.0.0-draft.10: which argument or parameter of the operation read this input (for example `values` and `weights`). The order of `inputs` is not significant, so without this field a record of an operation that reads two datasets in two roles cannot say which played which: swapping them changes the numbers and leaves two records that differ only in file names.

environment.description: Since 1.0.0-draft.10: the configuration that changed how THIS input was read (a sidecar, a georeferencing source), with the meaning of the record-level `environment` narrowed to one file. The record-level field keeps what applies to the whole run.

path.description: The output dataset this manifest describes, same path rules as inputs.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the output's bytes at the moment the manifest was written. For a shapefile or a `.gdb` directory, since 1.0.0-draft.9, the SHA-256 of the listing of its member files that section 3.3 defines.

crs.description: RECOMMENDED. The coordinate reference system the written dataset declares. Section 3.7 says the output CRS belongs here and not in crs_decisions; before 1.0.0-draft.4 there was nowhere here to put it. Omit it rather than predict it: a producer that has not written the file yet does not know.

layer.description: RECOMMENDED since 1.0.0-draft.9. The dataset inside a container that this record describes. When the output is a layer of a container, sha256 covers the whole container (section 3.3), so without this field two records for two layers of one container describe the same digest and nothing tells them apart.

output.description: RECOMMENDED. The digest of the dataset this record sits beside. Without it, a consumer cannot verify that the sidecar describes the bytes next to it — and the record cannot be wrapped in an in-toto attestation, whose subject requires a digest. Recommended rather than mandatory only because a producer may emit the manifest before the output is durably on disk; when it can be computed, it should be.

version.description: Which build produced the numbers. Algorithms change between releases, and so do their outputs; an engine without a version is not reproducible, only imitable.

engine.description: The software that computed the result — the engine, not the orchestrator that called it.

verification.description: Deterministic checks that ran on the result, recorded whether they passed or failed. At least one: a manifest with no checks at all is a log entry wearing a manifest's clothes. Failed checks MUST be recorded rather than suppressed — the audit trail has to survive the error it documents.

name.description: A stable code a consumer can branch on. MUST be one of the core names in section 3.6 of the specification, or an extension named `x-<producer>:<name>`. A name that is neither is a conformance error: an unconstrained vocabulary makes two records incomparable, which is the point of having a format.

detail.description: What was observed, in enough words to argue with. A bare boolean is a score, not a record.

critical.description: Whether a failure of this check should have stopped the pipeline. Optional; absent means the producer makes no claim.

argument.description: Which input or parameter the check is about. Without it, two inputs produce identically named entries that a consumer indexing by name collapses.

started_at.description: When the operation started, RFC 3339, UTC only (`Z`). Local times make two manifests disagree about the order of events depending on where they are read.

finished_at.description: When it finished, same form. MUST NOT precede started_at (checked semantically; a pattern cannot).

crs_decisions.description: RECOMMENDED. Coordinate-system decisions and the reason for each. `analysis_crs` and `reason` are strings; `source_crs` and `target_crs` are strings or null; `transformation` and `round_trip` are objects of the shapes defined here; a key this section does not define may hold a value of any type, because the question a consumer most needs answered here (was the transformation a ballpark one?) has to be answerable in a form a program can branch on. Section 3.7 fixes the keys, and since 1.0.0-draft.7 any other key MUST be named `x-<producer>:<name>`, the grammar of an extension check name. `round_trip` is the only name for a completed CRS round trip; a prefixed name for the same fact does not conform.

analysis_crs.description: The coordinate system the operation actually computed in.

reason.description: Why that system, in words a reader can check, naming the alternative rejected where there was one.

source_crs.description: The CRS the coordinates were in before the operation.

target_crs.description: The CRS they were put into, when the operation transformed them.

pipeline.description: The transformation operation string the engine used.

accuracy_m.description: The transformation's stated accuracy in metres, or null when the engine states none.

is_ballpark.description: True when no datum transformation was available and the engine treated the datums as equivalent. A boolean and not prose: a consumer has to be able to branch on it.

better_available_m.description: The stated accuracy, in metres, of a published operation that exists for this pair but was not used - normally because the grid file is not installed. Meaningful only when is_ballpark is true. It is the only field that separates 'no datum transformation exists for this pair' from 'one exists and this machine has not got it': the first is a fact about the world, the second is a download.

transformation.description: How the coordinates were transformed. Section 3.7.
The outbound leg: the caller's CRS to analysis_crs, as the engine reported it for that direction.

return_transformation.description: The return leg: analysis_crs back to the caller's CRS, as the engine reported it for THAT direction. Not derived from the outbound leg: even on WGS 84 to a UTM zone the two are different records, the projection and its inverse, so a copy of the outbound record names the wrong operation.

round_trip.description: The operation computed in analysis_crs and wrote its output back in the caller's CRS. New in 1.0.0-draft.6. MUST be written only once the output is back in the caller's CRS, and MUST NOT appear on a record written for a trip that did not complete. Section 3.7.

notes.description: RECOMMENDED. Disclosures about how inputs were handled before the engine saw them (workarounds, plain copies, normalisations).

check.description: Which check the repair was made for, named as in `verification[].name`. It may name a check that appears in no entry of `verification[]`: a repair applied to an INPUT happens before anything is verified, so the name is the only thing a consumer has to look it up by.

action.description: What was done, in the producer's own words. REQUIRED, and nullable on purpose: null says a repair was attempted and achieved nothing, with `error` saying why, while an absent key cannot be told apart from a producer that did not record it. A repair entry that does not say what was done discloses nothing, which is the one thing this field exists to prevent.

error.description: Why the repair failed, when it did. Null or absent when it did not.

resolved.description: Whether the check passed after the repair. False with a non-null `action` is the case worth reading: something was changed and the problem remained.

items.description: One disclosed repair. The four names below have fixed meaning as of 1.0.0-draft.5; since 1.0.0-draft.8 any other key MUST be named `x-<producer>:<name>` (section 3.4).

repairs.description: RECOMMENDED. Mechanical repairs applied to the output, each one disclosed. An undisclosed repair makes the manifest describe a file that never existed. Since 1.0.0-draft.5 the shape of an entry is fixed: before that the schema said only `type: object`, so two producers recording the same repair could share no key and both conform.

parameters_redacted.description: RECOMMENDED. True when redaction changed anything in this record. A manifest that silently differs from what ran is a worse defect than the secret it protects.

producer.description: RECOMMENDED. The software that emitted this record, as distinct from the engine that computed the result.

environment.description: RECOMMENDED. The configuration that influenced the result and lives neither in the data nor in the call: PROJ_NETWORK, GDAL_* variables, a project-level ellipsoid, the presence of a datum grid. Not AREA_OR_POINT: that is a tag inside the file, so it is data; a producer's reading of it goes in crs_decisions. The correct answer is not a number, it is this number with this configuration. Section 3.8.
